stem:
The unicellular fungus *Kluyveromyces lactis* is found in dairy products. It is a safe microorganism to culture for the extraction of the enzyme lactase. Lactase catalyses the breakdown of lactose, a sugar found in milk.

The reaction catalysed by lactase is summarised in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

Fig. 3.1

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the reaction that is catalysed by lactase. Use Fig. 3.1 to help you.

In your answer, identify **R** and product **S**.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
On a commercial scale, immobilised lactase can be used to produce lactose-free milk.

One of the products of the reaction shown in Fig. 3.1 acts as an inhibitor of lactase. This is an example of product inhibition.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Suggest why product inhibition is useful in *K. lactis* when lactase is acting as an intracellular enzyme, but can be a disadvantage when extracted lactase is used free in solution for the production of lactose-free milk.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest how using immobilised lactase in a commercial application helps to reduce the problem of product inhibition.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The first large-scale production of lactose-free milk with an immobilised enzyme used lactase trapped in cellulose triacetate fibres.

Suggest **one** feature of cellulose triacetate that makes it useful as an immobilising material.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
For a commercial application using an enzyme, the progress of the enzyme-catalysed reaction needs to be studied.

Outline how the progress of an enzyme-catalysed reaction can be investigated experimentally.
